report.summary: Imports module: extract_imports, tree-sitter and regex fallback, per-language parsing, internal/external resolution groundwork.

extract_imports docstring | low | Claims 'kind' distinction is syntactic for languages that mark it, but the code does not show the _parse_import function which assigns kind. | Inspect _parse_import to confirm it uses syntax to determine internal/external.

_CANDIDATE_LANGS docstring | low | Claims dotted-name languages have no syntactic marker, but Go imports can be quoted strings (stdlib vs external) – the regex fallback for Go captures quoted strings and parentheses, but kind assignment is not shown. | Check _parse_import for Go handling.

handoff.purpose: Define extract_imports and helper functions for non-Python import extraction with tree-sitter and regex fallback.

symbols.name: _CANDIDATE_LANGS
symbols.note: Set of languages where every import is treated as internal candidate.

symbols.name: _JS_EXTS
symbols.note: Tuple of file extensions and index paths for JS/TS resolution.

symbols.name: extract_imports
symbols.note: Main extraction function; returns list of (raw, kind) for non-Python files.

symbols.name: _ts_import_nodes
symbols.note: Extract import node texts using tree-sitter AST walk.

symbols.name: _REGEX_FALLBACK
symbols.note: Dictionary mapping language names to regex patterns for import detection.

symbols.name: _STR
symbols.note: Regex to extract quoted strings from import nodes.

claims.text: Python keeps its precise ``parse.python_imports`` path (relative-import resolution intact); THIS module handles every OTHER language so ``index.py`` can build a dependency graph + fan-in beyond Python.
claims.why: This claim refers to parse.python_imports and index.py, which are not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``extract_imports`` — find the import edges. With tree-sitter installed it walks the grammar's ``import_types`` nodes (precise node boundaries); without it, a per-language regex fallback keeps the edges flowing at lower precision.
claims.why: The function extract_imports checks tree_sitter_available and spec.import_types, calls _ts_import_nodes, and falls back to _regex_import_nodes.

claims.text: Each edge is ``(raw, kind)`` where ``kind`` is 'internal' (a resolution candidate — a repo-local module) or 'external' (a library / stdlib import).
claims.why: The assignment of 'internal'/'external' is done in _parse_import, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``resolve_internal`` — map an internal ``raw`` to an actual repo file by path/suffix match against the known file set.
claims.why: The function resolve_internal is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The ``kind`` distinction is syntactic where a language marks it (C ``"x"`` vs ``<x>``, Rust ``crate::``/``self::``/``super::``, JS relative ``./x``, QML quoted dir imports); for the dotted-name languages that give NO syntactic internal/external signal (Java, Kotlin, C#, PHP, Go) every import is treated as an internal *candidate* and the file-set match is the real arbiter.
claims.why: The logic for syntactic distinction and treating dotted-name languages as candidates is in _parse_import and _CANDIDATE_LANGS, but the actual implementation of kind assignment is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Python returns [] — it is resolved precisely by ``parse.python_imports`` in ``index.py``.
claims.why: In the code, if spec is None or spec.name == 'python', extract_imports returns [].

claims.text: Raw source text of every ``import_types`` node (precise boundaries).
claims.why: The function iterates over AST nodes of types in spec.import_types and extracts the source text using byte offsets.

claims.text: Iterative pre-order walk. A recursive one blows Python's recursion limit on deeply nested real-world ASTs (long chained/generated expressions) — push children reversed so they pop back in source order.
claims.why: The code uses a stack with reversed children to avoid recursion.

claims.text: Per-language fallback line patterns (no tree-sitter). Best-effort by design.
claims.why: _REGEX_FALLBACK is defined with regex patterns for each language, and _regex_import_nodes uses it.

observations.what: extract_imports returns [] for Python, but the docstring claims Python is handled precisely by parse.python_imports. That module is not in this chunk.
The constant _JS_EXTS is defined but not used in this chunk. It likely belongs to resolve_internal.

The regex for Go imports captures quoted strings and parentheses, but Go imports can also be grouped with parentheses; the regex uses re.S to match multiline, but may not handle all cases (e.g., named imports).
The _STR regex is defined but not used in this chunk; it is likely used in _parse_import.
